key_insight: The quadratic compute/memory bottleneck in offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction comes from variable-length Key-Value (KV) geometry representations; distilling that KV space into a fixed-size MLP via test-time training removes the growth and yields scalable inference.
problem_solved: Offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods scale poorly: compute and memory increase roughly quadratically with the number of input images, limiting applicability to large multi-view datasets.
method: Represent scene geometry as a variable-length KV space and learn to distill it into a compact, fixed-size Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP).
Perform test-time training (T^3) to transfer per-scene KV information into the fixed MLP, preserving fidelity while bounding memory/compute.
Use the distilled fixed-size MLP at inference to enable feed-forward reconstruction whose cost no longer grows with image count.
impact: Enables practical, memory- and compute-efficient offline 3D reconstruction at scale, making large multi-view pipelines faster and deployable on constrained hardware without sacrificing reconstruction quality.
visual_elements: Schematic: KV space (variable-length) → test-time distillation → fixed-size MLP (compact) showing reduced representation size
Performance chart: memory and runtime vs. number of images, comparing quadratic growth (baseline) to flat/linear behavior (VGG-T^3)
Before/After reconstructions: side-by-side 3D scenes reconstructed by a baseline KV method and by VGG-T^3 to show quality parity
Pipeline diagram: training (KV extraction + T^3) and inference (feed-forward MLP) with icons for images, GPU/memory, and model
paper_title: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale
paper_authors: Sven Elflein, Ruilong Li, Sérgio Agostinho, Zan Gojcic, Laura Leal-Taixé
